steps.description: Read /eval-four-arms-without-paired-n5-2/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12000 genes x 11 columns; first column is the gene symbol, remaining 10 are samples) and /eval-four-arms-without-paired-n5-2/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (10 rows x 3 columns: sample, subject, condition). steps.name: Paired DE: treated vs control blocked on subject
caveats: With 5 pairs, apparent significance can be driven by one subject — the per-pair sign-consistency table is the guard against this and must be reported for the headline genes
Dispersion estimates with ~4 residual df are unstable; if the dispersion fit looks degenerate, report the dispersion plot and say so
If subject effects are very strong, some genes may be significant with tiny absolute fold changes — report effect sizes alongside padj, not padj alone
Gene symbols may contain duplicates or non-standard entries; report how any duplicate symbols were handled
steps.context: Paired design with 5 subjects. Blocking on subject removes between-subject baseline expression differences, which in blood are large (cell-composition and genotype driven) and would otherwise swamp the treatment effect. With 5 pairs the residual degrees of freedom are ~4, so dispersion estimation is the limiting factor and DESeq2's shared-dispersion shrinkage is doing real work.
steps.question: Which genes change significantly between the treated and control blood sample within subjects, when subject is used as a blocking factor across the 5 pairs, and how consistent is each gene's response across the individual pairs?
constraints: Do NOT run an unpaired treated-vs-control comparison as the primary analysis — subject must be in the design
Use Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment; report padj, never raw p-values, as the significance criterion
Shrunken LFCs are for ranking and visualisation; significance must come from the unshrunken Wald test padj
Do not select the significance threshold after seeing the results — report the pre-specified padj<0.05 result first, and any relaxed threshold explicitly as exploratory
Per-pair values must come from normalized or VST counts, not raw counts
steps.description: Fit the DESeq2 model with design ~ subject + condition on the filtered DESeqDataSet from T1S1 and run the Wald test for the treated-vs-control contrast (control as reference). Report the full results table sorted by adjusted p-value with baseMean, log2FoldChange, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj. Apply LFC shrinkage (apeglm on the condition coefficient; ashr if the coefficient form makes apeglm unavailable) and save shrunken LFCs for ranking. Define significant genes at padj < 0.05 and report the count both with and without an additional |LFC| >= 1 filter; if fewer than ~10 genes pass padj < 0.05, also report the padj < 0.1 set and say plainly that the study is underpowered rather than lowering the threshold silently. For the top ~50 genes by padj, compute per-subject log2 ratios from VST or normalized counts (treated minus control within each subject) and tabulate them, plus a count of how many of the 5 pairs share the sign of the overall effect — this is the direct answer to 'within each subject'. Produce: MA plot, volcano plot (labelled with top genes), a heatmap of the top ~40 genes on VST values with columns ordered by subject then condition, and per-pair line/slope plots for the top ~12 genes. As a sensitivity check, fit limma-voom with the same ~ subject + condition design and report the overlap of the padj<0.05 sets and the Spearman correlation of the two t-statistic/LFC rankings; state disagreements rather than reporting only the union. Save the full ranked result table (all genes, with shrunken LFC) for T1S3.

Outputs a full per-gene result table for all retained genes with baseMean, raw and shrunken log2FoldChange, pvalue, and padj (BH)
Reports the number of genes at padj<0.05, at padj<0.05 & |LFC|>=1, and at padj<0.1, with the underpowered case stated in plain words if the significant set is small or empty
Provides a per-subject (per-pair) log2 change table for the top genes plus the count of pairs agreeing in sign with the overall effect
Produces MA plot, volcano plot, top-gene VST heatmap ordered by subject and condition, and per-pair slope plots for the leading genes
Reports the limma-voom paired sensitivity fit alongside DESeq2, including overlap of significant sets and rank correlation, with disagreements named

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of the paired treatment response
caveats: With a small DE set, ORA results are unstable and can hinge on a handful of genes — prefer the GSEA result and say which one is being relied on
GO parent and child terms share members, so significant hits arrive in correlated blocks; a raw count of significant terms overstates the finding
Enrichment does not establish mechanism — leading-edge overlap with T1S2 top genes is the honest way to connect the two, not a causal claim
steps.context: Whole-blood transcriptome, so immune, interferon, inflammatory, and heme/erythrocyte-related sets are the plausible responders and also the plausible artefacts — a shift in blood cell composition between draws can produce pathway-level signal that is not a within-cell transcriptional response. Say so when such sets come up. Required reference data: human hallmark gene sets, human GO biological process sets, and human WikiPathways, all keyed on gene symbols; these are annotation, and if a collection is unavailable at run time the step should report the gap and proceed with whichever collections are present.
steps.question: Which biological processes and pathways are coordinately shifted by treatment in blood, based on the subject-blocked treated-vs-control gene ranking?
constraints: Use human (Homo sapiens) gene sets only — the data are human blood
Use gene-symbol-keyed gene sets to match the HGNC symbols in counts.csv; if any ID mapping is done, report how many genes failed to map
Background universe for ORA is the set of genes tested in T1S2, not all annotated genes
Do not report nominal enrichment p-values as significant findings — use BH-adjusted values
Do not use mouse or rat pathway resources
steps.description: Take the full ranked gene table from T1S2 and run gene-set analysis for the treatment response. Primary method: GSEA (fgsea or gseapy prerank) on all retained genes ranked by the shrunken log2 fold change (or by -log10(p) signed by LFC direction, stated explicitly), which remains informative when the FDR-significant gene list is too small for over-representation testing — the expected situation with 5 pairs. Secondary method: over-representation analysis of the padj<0.05 gene set (split into up and down in treated), run only if that set has at least ~15 genes; if it does not, report that ORA was skipped and why. Gene sets: human MSigDB hallmark, human GO biological process, and human WikiPathways — all HGNC-symbol GMTs, matching the symbol identifiers in counts.csv, so no ID conversion should be needed; report the fraction of ranked genes that match each collection's symbol space and note any collection where the match rate is poor. Report leading-edge genes for the top enriched sets and cross-reference them against the top DE genes from T1S2. Collapse redundant parent/child GO terms before reporting a term count.

States the ranking statistic used and why, and reports the symbol match rate against each gene-set collection
Runs over-representation analysis on the padj<0.05 up and down sets using the tested genes as background, or explicitly reports that it was skipped because the set was too small
Collapses redundant GO terms before reporting, and reports a de-duplicated term count
Names any requested gene-set collection that was unavailable at run time and continues with the remaining ones rather than failing
Flags enriched sets that are plausibly explained by blood cell-composition differences rather than a transcriptional treatment response

plan.title: Paired treated-vs-control DE in 5 subjects (blood RNA-seq)
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a 12,000-gene x 11-column raw integer count matrix (counts.csv, gene symbols in the first column, star_featurecounts) with a 10-row x 3-column sample table (metadata.csv: sample, subject, condition). Design is a balanced paired design: 5 human subjects, each contributing one control and one treated blood sample. The counts file has 11 columns because the first is the gene-symbol column, so exactly 10 count columns must align 1:1 with the 10 metadata rows — this must be verified before modelling, since a mismatch silently mislabels the pairing.

The research question — which genes respond to treatment within each subject — is exactly a within-subject (paired) contrast. The correct model therefore blocks on subject: ~ subject + condition in DESeq2, so that between-subject baseline variation is absorbed and the condition coefficient tests the within-pair treatment shift. Ignoring the pairing would be the single largest avoidable loss of power here, and with n=5 pairs that power is already thin.

T1S1 loads and validates the two files, checks the paired structure (each subject exactly one control and one treated), builds the DESeq2 object with the paired design, and produces sample-level QC (library sizes, VST PCA coloured by subject and condition, sample-correlation heatmap, within-pair distances). This step decides whether pairing actually explains variance — if PC1 separates subjects, the paired design is empirically justified; if a pair is discordant with the rest, that must be reported, not hidden.

T1S2 runs the paired DESeq2 Wald test for treated vs control with subject as a blocking factor, applies apeglm/ashr LFC shrinkage for ranking, and writes the full result table plus the significant-gene list. It also reports the per-subject log2 fold change for each top gene (paired per-pair values), which is what makes the 'within each subject' part of the question answerable: a gene with a consistent sign across all 5 pairs is far stronger evidence than one driven by a single subject. A limma-voom paired sensitivity fit (duplicate-free, blocked on subject) is run alongside to check that hits are not an artefact of one modelling choice.

T1S3 takes the ranked gene list and runs pathway enrichment against staged human MSigDB hallmark and GO-BP sets plus human WikiPathways, using GSEA on the full shrunken-LFC ranking (not just the thresholded list), because with 5 pairs the FDR-significant gene set may be small and a rank-based test remains informative when an over-representation test has nothing to work with. This step is annotation: if the reference sets were absent it would report that and the DE result would still stand.

Honest limits stated up front: n=5 pairs is small. Expect modest detection power, wide LFC intervals, and sensitivity to a single outlier pair. The plan therefore emphasises per-pair consistency and effect sizes over a headline count of significant genes.
